tradition_kind.cult: cult of a deity (within a wider religion)
tradition_kind.arch: archaeological or reconstructed horizon (beliefs inferred from material remains or comparative linguistics)

tradition_status.R: revived or reconstructed in modern times
tradition_status.H: historical phase that evolved into a successor tradition

date_confidence.H: high: well documented or precisely dated
date_confidence.M: medium: scholarly consensus within the stated range

presence_event.state: adopted by a ruler or state
presence_event.major: becomes the majority or dominant religion

interaction_type.reform: target is a reform movement within or against source
interaction_type.conflict: violent conflict between source and target
interaction_type.transmission: texts or teachings of source carried into target's world
interaction_type.convert: mass conversion from source to target
interaction_type.revive: target is a modern revival of source

site_until.blank: still standing or in religious use
site_until.year: end of religious use (abandonment, destruction or conversion)
site_until.same as start: a single event, e.g. one burial

meta.name: World Religion Atlas
meta.year_convention: Signed integers: negative = BCE, positive = CE. There is no year 0 (1 BCE = -1, 1 CE = 1).
meta.date_ranges: *_start = earliest year of the scholarly window, *_latest = latest; equal means a precise date.
meta.presence_rule: At year Y a tradition is present at a row's location if year_start <= Y and (year_end IS NULL or year_end >= Y).
meta.coordinates: WGS84 decimal degrees. Specific places are approximate to ~10 km; country rows use an approximate centroid.
meta.year_range: Years run from -500000 to the build year.
meta.prominence: Presence prominence 1-5 is an approximate share of the local population, not a count; see code_lists.
meta.language: All names, titles and notes are in English; name_original / title_original hold native-language forms where given.
